text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller is scheduled to meet European Union ministers on January 29.
- The government coalition hinges on common positions concerning the Cyprus problem but nothing else, says junior partner Spyros Kyprianou, leader of the centre-right Diko party.
- Members of the right-wing Disy party accuse the presidential palace of encouraging members to rebel against the party line in municipal elections last month.
- Police turn a blind eye to behaviour of one of its members who owns a gambling club and runs a protection racket in Nicosia.
- President Glafcos Clerides is expected to intervene to smooth over relations between Diko and Disy parties.
- Labour ministry plans to halt employment permits for foriegn nurses.
- Greece's Education Minister Gerrasimos Arsenis proposes a pact between Cyprus and Greece to modernise the education system.
